author: jade-cho
title: Debian Packages job fails apt-get update/install with DNS resolution errors on Ubuntu mirrors

root_cause: The 'Debian Packages' job's container could not resolve DNS for any of the configured Ubuntu apt mirrors (azure.archive.ubuntu.com, archive.ubuntu.com, security.ubuntu.com) during 'apt-get update', spending ~4 minutes retrying before all sources failed. Because the package index was empty/stale, the subsequent 'apt-get install openvino' step could not locate transitive dependencies (gnupg, wget, ca-certificates) and failed with exit code 100. This is a transient DNS/network resolution outage in the runner's container networking or the upstream mirror infrastructure, unrelated to the merged PR #39638 (a GPU FakeQuantize precompute fix) which only touches intel_gpu C++ sources.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reproducible outside CI; this is a transient DNS resolution failure in the GitHub Actions runner/container network reaching Ubuntu apt mirrors. Locally, running `apt-get update && apt-get install openvino` inside the same ubuntu:24.04 container with working DNS would succeed.
recommended_actions: Re-run the 'Debian Packages' job (post-commit doctor does not auto-rerun; a maintainer should trigger a workflow re-run) since this is a transient infrastructure issue.
Consider adding a retry-with-backoff wrapper around 'apt-get update' in job_debian_packages.yml to tolerate transient DNS failures from Ubuntu mirrors.
Monitor GitHub Actions runner status page for networking incidents around 2026-11-11T14:03-14:07Z if this recurs frequently.
prevention_strategies: Wrap apt-get update/install steps with a retry loop (e.g., 3 attempts with exponential backoff) in the Debian Packages job definition to absorb transient DNS/mirror outages without failing the whole post-commit run. Consider pinning a more reliable mirror or using apt's `Acquire::Retries` option.
historical_context: Related but distinct Network-category Debian Packages failures have occurred before with different root symptoms: pattern 23eeaa0c051f425e ('File has unexpected size' on archive.ubuntu.com, 2026-10-22) and pattern ad3678610dab3215 ('Hash Sum mismatch' on archive.ubuntu.com, 2026-10-22). This is the first recorded occurrence of a pure DNS resolution failure ('Temporary failure resolving') against all three Ubuntu mirror hosts simultaneously, suggesting a runner-level network/DNS issue rather than a mirror content inconsistency.
